label: Definition
subgoals: Test whether A maps v onto its own line
Write the scaling relation Av = lambda v
Reject the zero vector as an eigenvector

visual.title: An eigenvector is a direction that does not turn
visual.caption: Drag v around the circle. Where A v stays on the same line, the direction is an eigenvector and v·Av is its eigenvalue.

predict.question: For A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]], the direction (1, 1) is special because A does what to it?
options: Keeps it on the same line
predict.explain: A(1, 1) = (3, 3), which is 3 times (1, 1): same direction, scaled by the eigenvalue 3.

label: The characteristic equation
subgoals: Subtract lambda down the diagonal of A
Expand det(A - lambda I) into the characteristic polynomial
Solve for the lambdas scaling each direction

label: Eigenspaces
subgoals: Plug each lambda into (A - lambda I)v = 0
Parametrize the solution set for v
Collect the lines fixed by A
